title: Shallow token-hash prefetch and parallel ingest lane for prompt preprocessing
creator: Nina Cho
description: Problem: Prefill-side overhead for high-concurrency workloads is dominated by: (1) repeated UTF-8 normalization and lexical analysis for common prompt prefixes, (2) hash-table lookups for cached tokenizations that currently require heavy locking, and (3) single-threaded preprocessing lanes that block when upstream I/O or small-block allocations occur. This ticket introduces a shallow token-hash prefetch layer and a parallel ingest lane to reduce per-request prefill CPU and tail latency.
acceptance_criteria: 1) 95th-percentile prefill latency reduced by >=30% on benchmark 'chat-sim-small-p50k' at 8k RPS; 2) CPU time spent in tokenizer functions reduced by >=40% for repeat-prefix workloads; 3) No regression in output tokenization correctness (existing token-roundtrip tests pass); 4) Graceful fallback to existing tokenizer cache when memory pressure occurs.
design_notes: Approach: add a small per-worker shallow-prefetch table keyed by 64-bit rolling token-hash (not full byte-string) to capture repeated prefixes and their partial tokenization frames. The prefetch table is lock-stripable per-core and stores an immutable small object: (prefix-length, kv-cache-hint, vectorized-normalization-state). On request ingress, do a fast-path check: compute rolling hash on first N bytes (configurable, default 64 bytes) using a SIMD-accelerated window; if hit, fast-apply the cached partial token span and resume tokenization from that offset. Concurrently, move UTF-8 normalization and splitting into a parallel ingest lane using a work-stealing bounded queue so short-blocking operations don't stall the main event loop. Kernel/attention interaction: by reducing effective prefill CPU, we aim to increase opportunity for batching and better kernel selection downstream (longer sequence aggregation within the same GPU epoch). Memory curation: entries are ephemeral and sized to stay under worker-local budget; eviction is LRU-ish via timestamp buckets to avoid global locking.
implementation_plan:
- Phase 1 (spike): 2d prototype of 64-byte rolling hash + lock-stripable per-core table (Ravi) — 3d
- Phase 2: integrate SIMD normalization into ingest lane; add work-stealing queue (Anita) — 5d
- Phase 3: correctness tests, token-roundtrip, and fuzzing; benchmark harness integration (Marcus) — 4d
- Phase 4: gradual rollout behind runtime flag, monitor cost/latency dashboards, enable canary for 10% traffic then ramp (SRE-runbook) — 3d
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: false-positive hash collisions causing incorrect prefix reuse. Mitigation: validate cached span by verifying raw bytes match up to prefix-length before applying; fall back on full tokenization on mismatch. Risk: memory amplification under pathological workloads. Mitigation: tunable worker budget and circuit-breaker to disable prefetch when RSS or allocator pressure crosses threshold. Risk: increased CPU due to extra hashing for short unique prompts. Mitigation: only compute rolling hash for requests > min_length and sample dynamic bypass heuristics based on recent hit-rate.
benchmarks: Bench harness: https://bench.redwood.internal/runtime/prefill/ingest/compare. Current baseline (2026-03-01): 95th prefill latency 22ms @ 8k RPS. Target after change: ~15ms p95. Microbench: tokenizer CPU time per-request (median) baseline 2.8ms.
